takeaway: Hot, sticky Thursday with Tropical Wave #48 nearby: morning partly cloudy, then scattered afternoon showers and storms in northern Pacific Costa Rica. Surf winds stay Pacific/onshore (west–northwest today, then west to southwest through the weekend) — expect choppier faces; early checks only, not all-day glass. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a high chance of forming later this week into next. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu–Sat)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says lower pressure across Central America is drawing the Pacific moisture band closer, and Tropical Wave #48 is passing today (Thursday), adding instability. Pacífico Norte today: partly cloudy morning, then partly cloudy with scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms; Nicoya heat stays sharp (around 35°C). Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate — typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine — with European means a bit quieter than the U.S. average on Thursday into Friday. The official longer outlook still keeps northern Pacific Costa Rica on the drier-than-normal side for this week (roughly 5–90 mm Pacífico Norte for 28 Sep–4 Oct). Near-surface Papagayo winds: west–northwest about 10 kt today; Friday light/variable at Papagayo with west elsewhere; Saturday similar light/variable Papagayo and west elsewhere.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before scattered afternoon storms. Expect strong heat and sticky air. For surf, treat Thursday–Saturday as Pacific/onshore–side days: west–northwest fading to west, with Papagayo often light/variable Friday–Saturday — that is not glassy all-day offshore. Early checks only.
periods.confidence: High that Thursday is a Wave #48 / Pacific-moisture day with scattered afternoon storms and no nearby cyclone threat. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how firmly Friday–Saturday west/onshore holds at the beach.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun–Wed)
periods.pattern: Official weekly guidance still expects rains more dispersed overall after the wave pulse, with Pacífico Norte remaining quieter than peak rainy-season weeks. Ensemble averages show continued moist Pacific-side days into early next week — often light to moderate daily totals near Nicoya — without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Longer official outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal into early October. Marine winds trend southwest by Sunday, then south to southwest Monday. A new East Pacific low could form south of southern Mexico late weekend / early next week and drift west-northwest away from Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Keep weekend and early-week plans flexible for quick storms. Surf-wind quality looks weaker than trade-offshore days: expect more Pacific/southwest–south flow and choppier faces, with only early checks for any leftover glass. Nicaragua is not showing a clean all-day offshore signal for Nosara mornings in this window.
periods.confidence: Moderate for a quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte theme after today’s wave pulse; low–moderate on exact wet-day timing and how firmly weekend–early-week onshore winds hold.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from early into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for the current week. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into mid-October, and the U.S. tropics outlook notes a chance of a broader Central American rain-gyre pattern early in its week-2 window (around Oct 7 onward) — worth watching, not a locked-in flood spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west; formation odds south of southern Mexico are now high through seven days.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes; re-check midweek if a gyre signal firms up.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail and for any week-2 gyre risk past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused gyre window over Costa Rica now; Wave #48 is a Thursday pulse, not a multi-day stuck rain machine. Broader week-2 (around Oct 7+) gyre mention in U.S. tropics guidance remains a longer-range watch only.
gyreWatch.supporting: Lower pressure across Central America is drawing the Pacific moisture band closer. Tropical Wave #48 passes today with added instability. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means keep light-to-moderate Pacific-side rain into early next week. U.S. tropics outlook notes model support for a possible Central American gyre early in week-2. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Thursday Pacífico Norte forecast is only scattered afternoon showers under Wave #48 / Pacific-moisture factors. Longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific / onshore (W–NW Thu → W Fri–Sat → SW–S Sun–Mon)
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters: west–northwest about 10 kt today with scattered showers. Tonight west about 10 kt. Friday light/variable at Papagayo with west about 10 kt elsewhere; Saturday similar light/variable Papagayo and west elsewhere; Sunday southwest about 10 kt; Monday south about 10 kt. Mid-level maps are mixed (U.S. ensemble means lean west–southwest near Nicoya; European means sometimes show more easterly aloft over Nicaragua) — trust the marine surface call for beach wind. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as glassy all-day offshore. Nicaragua is not offering a clear all-day offshore quality signal for Nosara this stretch.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early checks only Thursday–Monday. Expect choppier Pacific/onshore–side flow most of the day. No clean all-day offshore / Caribbean-trade signal this period.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the marine forecast trend (west–northwest today, then west and southwest through the weekend). Moderate on exact hour-to-hour beach winds Friday–Saturday as Papagayo goes light/variable.

whatChanged: Tropical Wave #48 is now today’s story (Thursday), not a late-week maybe — daily regional guidance leads the lagging weekly wording. Surf winds stay Pacific/onshore: west–northwest today, west Friday–Saturday, southwest–south Sunday–Monday — no brief NE/offshore pulse like yesterday morning. Newest official storm notice is Wed 30 Sep 10:20 a.m. (Pacific moisture band reactivating; Pacífico Norte storms more isolated). Genesis chance south of southern Mexico jumped to high (~70% in 7 days) from medium (~40%) yesterday. Active East Pacific systems remain Hurricane Rachel (near Mexico), Tropical Depression Nineteen-E (far west), and Tropical Storm Nolo (near Hawaii) — none threaten Costa Rica. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only.
practical: Best outdoors: Thursday morning before scattered afternoon storms; expect strong inland heat and sticky Pacific-side humidity. For surf, treat today through the weekend as Pacific/onshore — early checks only; light/variable Papagayo is not all-day glass. Wave #48 is a Thursday pulse, not a multi-day washout. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline. Latest official storm notice: Wed 30 Sep 10:20 a.m. — Pacific moisture band reactivating; Pacífico Norte storms more isolated.
